purpose: Determine whether the current painterly mythic dark-fantasy direction and Purple Haze signature can read as an in-game style at 1024x1024 before committing to full production.
scope: One generated 1024x1024 Haze-combat concept integrated into a temporary Godot 4.7.2 GL Compatibility scene. This is visual proof, not a playable game, final art, or approval of the camera.

generation.workflow: Studio image.generate.klein; FLUX.2 Klein 4B Distilled FP8
generation.license_status: model source register describes 4B weights as Apache-2.0; separate weight/component terms and output rights not human-reviewed for release

godot.renderer: GL Compatibility / OpenGL 3.3 NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5070 Ti Laptop GPU

strengths: A coherent slate-blue dusk palette, ruined arch landmark, foreground framing and warm ember points make a readable mythic-fantasy place.
The violet lantern, plume and low cloud create a strong purple focal accent against the environment; the cloud is not opaque and the major silhouettes remain visible.

At the 1024-square proof scale, foreground character silhouettes, weapon direction and central action are immediately legible; the overall composition feels authored rather than a generic neon HUD scene.
defects: The enemy has a modern firearm-like ranged weapon, not the torch-bearing melee rogue described by the brief; this is a major subject compliance error.
The Haze ability appears as a small isolated magical puff/bolus between characters rather than a low, extended area-control cloud that communicates persistent battlefield coverage.
The elevated camera and character size/route read were not compared in a running playable scene against side-on; only one camera direction received this fresh generation.
Generated composition does not establish reusable identity, authored animation, responsive VFX, combat timing, navigation/collision, or feasible asset modularization.
Candidate remains an opaque background scene illustration and cannot directly serve as a transparent character, prop, tile, or animated effect asset.
agent_visual_critique.decision: Keep as an art-direction candidate, not approved. Strong enough to show the painterly dark-fantasy scene treatment and focal color contrast can work at gameplay-like framing, but it is not yet a valid Haze-combat design proof because the enemy weapon and cloud behavior violate the intended scene contract. Next visual iteration should fix these two defects while holding palette/camera/lighting constant; a fair camera decision still requires corresponding engine compositions.

quality_boundaries.agent_review: initial critique recorded; candidate needs prompt/subject iteration
